svg.text: LP-MSPM0G3507, seen from above, USB unplugged. Add the wires in the numbered order; each number sits at both ends of its wire and in the list below. The schematic shows the same circuit in symbols.
J1 and J2 are the outer columns, J3 and J4 the inner ones; pin 1, 21, 40 and 20 are at the USB end.
Wire colours: red 3.3 V, orange 5 V, black ground; every other colour is one signal.

g.text: Breadboard: holes a to e, and f to j, in one column are joined; each long rail is joined end to end.
Column 1 is at this end; rails and holes count up toward the top.
Wires, in the order you add them
Place first: Two-wheel chassis, Battery pack
Ground rail (blue, hole 2) to J3 pin 22 (GND)
Battery pack minus to Ground rail
Left driver motor power from the battery
Left driver VM, breadboard j9 to Battery pack plus
Left driver GND, breadboard j8 to Ground rail
Left driver STBY, breadboard j7 to 3V3 rail
Left driver AIN1, breadboard j6 to J4 pin 38 (PA28)
Left driver AIN2, breadboard j5 to J4 pin 37 (PA31)
Left driver AO1, breadboard j4 to Motor lead
Left driver AO2, breadboard j3 to Motor lead
Place first: Right DRV8833, Pick at the bench
Right driver motor power from the battery
Right driver VM, breadboard j21 to Battery pack plus
Right driver GND, breadboard j20 to Ground rail
Right driver STBY, breadboard j19 to 3V3 rail
Right driver AIN1, breadboard j18 to Pick at the bench
Right driver AIN2, breadboard j17 to Pick at the bench
Right driver AO1, breadboard j16 to Motor lead
Right driver AO2, breadboard j15 to Motor lead
Ranger GND, breadboard j25 to Ground rail
Ranger VCC, breadboard j28 to 3V3 rail
Ranger Trig, breadboard j27 to J4 pin 35 (PB13)
Ranger Echo, breadboard j26 to J4 pin 36 (PB20)
Left DRV8833: VM in g9, GND in g8, STBY in g7, AIN1 in g6, AIN2 in g5, AO1 in g4, AO2 in g3
Right DRV8833: VM in g21, GND in g20, STBY in g19, AIN1 in g18, AIN2 in g17, AO1 in g16, AO2 in g15
RCWL-1601 ranger: VCC in g28, TRIG in g27, ECHO in g26, GND in g25
Two-wheel chassis: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
Battery pack: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
Pick at the bench: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
Pick at the bench: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
The DRV8833 VM pin takes the motor supply (2.7 to 10.8 V); the logic pins are 3.3 V safe.
A yellow flag marked Pick at the bench is a LaunchPad pin chosen at the first run: the program prints which pin it uses, and the pin table then gets the number.
Then plug in USB, run the build, and expect
The wheels follow your hand; the LaunchPad does not reset when the motors start.

svg.text: Fox Red Labs. Pins from the build's pin table, the one the program is built from; the 3D build on the page shows the same wiring step by step. Board picture: TI SLAU873E, figure 1-1.
